lead: A week before the 4 November local elections, Durban is still gripped by anti-migrant attacks as the army's deployment nears its end, and a KZN councillor candidate has been arrested with an unlicensed gun. Abroad, Israel's election ended without a clear winner.

items.title: Durban anti-migrant attacks go on despite army and police presence
items.summary: Daily protests and assaults on foreign nationals continue in the CBD, Berea and Morningside. Four men have been charged, civic groups say the police response falls short, and the SANDF deployment is due to end on Saturday.

items.title: Councillor candidate arrested with unlicensed firearm near Durban
items.summary: Police arrested a 49-year-old candidate in the coming local elections at a home in Dassenhoek on Tuesday. He faces charges of illegally possessing a firearm and ammunition and is due in the Pinetown Magistrate's Court. His party was not named.

items.title: At least 43 suspected political killings this year, KZN worst hit
items.summary: A GI-TOC count shows at least 43 suspected politically motivated killings in the first nine months of 2026 and 10 more in October. KwaZulu-Natal recorded the most incidents, ahead of Gauteng. Analysts link the attacks to fights over council control and contracts.

items.title: Six killed in head-on crash on the N3 at Van Reenen's Pass
items.summary: A light delivery vehicle, reportedly carrying workers in its back, collided with a truck on Tuesday afternoon, and that truck then hit a second one. The RTMC is investigating the cause.

items.title: Election preparations on track, says Cogta minister Hlabisa
items.summary: Velenkosini Hlabisa said voting stations, staffing and security are ready for 4 November, with the ConCourt dispute over ANC candidate lists now settled. Separately, Cape Town mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis warned that smaller parties could push the city into a coalition.

items.title: uMshwathi villagers share river water with cattle
items.summary: Families in Swayimane in the KZN midlands say they have no taps and rely on a stream also used by livestock, while tankers seldom reach them. The municipality did not respond to EWN's questions.

items.title: De Kock blames prosecutors for failing to pursue apartheid crimes
items.summary: Testifying at the Khampepe inquiry, Eugene de Kock said the NPA never asked him for information, and he named former apartheid-era politicians he claims were involved in bombings. His claims have not been tested.

items.title: Ramaphosa weighing report on Iran's role in BRICS naval drills
items.summary: The Presidency says a panel has been investigating since February why Iran's participation in January's exercise off the west coast went beyond the observer role the president had set. The report remains confidential.

items.title: Israel's election ends without a clear winner, exit polls show
items.summary: Exit polls put Netanyahu's bloc and Eisenkot's bloc at about 51 seats each, with Arab parties near 18. Coalition talks are expected to take weeks, and a repeat election next year is possible.

items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases
items.summary: The DRC has recorded 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths in its worst outbreak yet. Kenya and Nigeria have also reported cases, and the WHO has started a first vaccine trial.

items.title: Egypt approves military help for Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
items.summary: Egypt's parliament authorised President Sisi to give Saudi Arabia military support after the Saudi-led coalition said it shot down Houthi missiles and drones fired at the kingdom.

items.title: Limited ceasefire holds in occupied Oleshky as Russia hits Kyiv
items.summary: Ukrainian and Russian officials say a local truce in Oleshky is allowing aid deliveries and evacuations. Only about 6,000 of its 24,000 former residents remain. Russian strikes hit infrastructure in Kyiv.

items.title: Gunmen kill at least 62 in north-eastern Nigeria
items.summary: An attack on a community last Friday left 62 dead and 52 wounded, and displaced thousands. In Ethiopia, the Orthodox Church says at least 60 people died in two attacks in Oromia over the past week.

items.title: JSE rises 0.6% while the rand hovers near R16.66
items.summary: The All Share closed at 109,820 on Tuesday, led by Naspers and AngloGold Ashanti. The rand is at its weakest since early October, weighed down by a firmer dollar and higher oil prices.

items.title: Fuel levy relief points to small petrol cut and bigger diesel cut in November
items.summary: Treasury's temporary levy cut of R1.50/l on petrol and R3/l on diesel outweighs under-recoveries. Data to 23 October pointed to 95 petrol about 23c cheaper and diesel about R1.70 lower, although the petrol margin is thin.

items.title: Kilometres-long truck queues at Durban port after storm
items.summary: Traffic to the port crawled on Tuesday as a severe thunderstorm added to existing backlogs at the Durban Gateway Terminal, which has struggled since a new operating system went live in August. Transnet had not commented.

items.title: Brent near $115 as Gulf tensions mount; Fed decides today
items.summary: Oil rose on reports the US asked Gulf states to prepare for possible new action against Iran, and on attacks on Saudi energy sites and Hormuz tankers. Markets see little chance of a Fed hike tonight but price one in December.

items.title: Starc's six wickets bowl Proteas out for 329 at Newlands
items.summary: After a 140-run opening stand, Marques Ackerman fell for 95 and Aiden Markram made 78, but Mitchell Starc took 6-72 to end South Africa's innings on day one of the series decider.

items.title: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or
items.summary: The Bayern Munich striker became the first Englishman to win in 25 years, ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal. Alexia Putellas took the women's award for a third time.

items.title: Bulls hold off Ulster 34-26 at Loftus
items.summary: A late Curwin Bosch penalty denied Ulster a bonus point. Coach Johan Ackermann wants answers on refereeing calls, and Handré Pollard picked up a hamstring injury.

items.title: Anthropic files for a stock market listing
items.summary: The AI company filed its prospectus on 26 October under the ticker ANT. It reported fast revenue growth and a large first-half loss driven mainly by a noncash charge. Reports suggest a valuation of $1.5-2 trillion.
